 Menu TV & Film 'Black Mirror' Season 8 Is Filming In England For Netflix
 T Troy Smith · November 18, 2026 Troy Smith Share f X in ✉ Season 8 of Netflix’s “Black Mirror” is in production in England, but the streamer has not said when it will arrive.
 Variety reported that filming began this summer, about 16 months after season 7 premiered on April 10, 2025.
 That is far shorter than the multiyear gaps the series once had. Creator Charlie Brooker is writing and executive producing with Bisha K. Ali, the creator of “Ms. Marvel.”
 One confirmed location is Hope Cove House, a hotel in the coastal village of Hope Cove, which is being dressed as the “Sandcastle Hotel.”
 Netflix has not announced a synopsis, episode titles, an episode count or an official cast. Emma Laird, known for “Mayor of Kingstown,” has been linked to the season, but that is not confirmed.
 Brooker announced the renewal in January, saying the show would return “just in time for reality to catch up with it.”
 Season 7 earned Golden Globe nominations for best limited or anthology series, as well as acting nods for Rashida Jones and Paul Giamatti. All seven existing seasons are streaming on Netflix.
